title: Diagnostics: ping, dig, nslookup, traceroute, mtr, netstat/ss and tcpdump

videos.script: Most calls about the network start the same way. The internet is down. The site does not open. The printer is not there. Each of those is a symptom, and the same symptom has a handful of causes, on different floors of the stack. {{symptoms}} This lesson is about finding the floor. You check from the bottom: the cable and the address, then the gateway, then a far address, then a name, then the service itself. The first check that fails is where the fault is. {{ladder}} You will work through tickets that were broken on purpose. A laptop with no way out. A DNS server that does not exist. A path that loses packets, and one that only looks like it does. A printer with somebody else's address. A web server that stopped. {{tickets}} On the way you will meet, side by side, the tools this whole course has been using. Ping, dig and nslookup, traceroute and mtr, ss, and tcpdump. And you will learn to read what each one says when it fails. {{tools}}
